column1: # Upstream skills — THE curated set, one manifest for both hosts (parity by construction).
#   Claude Code: install.sh keeps a shallow git checkout of the repo (pulled on session start by
#                sec-update → live), and sec-init links each listed skill into the app repo's
#                .claude/skills/ (git-excluded) → only these skills exist, so nothing duplicates.
#   Hermes:      hermes.sh installs each row through the skills hub (`hermes skills update` = live).
# Source: UnboundCompute/security-agent-skills (MIT) — 194 tool-agnostic white-box security skills.
#   Each is ONE vulnerability class, so they load only on their trigger and never tax other work.
#   Curated to "our sites and apps": web + API + mobile + the Marketing Kit's attack surface
#   (Resend webhooks, Telnyx callbacks, CRM DB, partner payouts). The kit's own skills
#   (skills/*) own the workflow + the stack specifics; these own the technique depth.
# Deliberately NOT installed: EVM/DeFi/blockchain, Windows/AD, Kubernetes/IoT/embedded, and the
#   enterprise directory/federation skills — none of them touch a web/API/mobile product.
# hosts: both | claude | hermes      trust: community (Hermes scanner decides) | official (--force)

column4: white-box master loop: orient → enumerate the taxonomy → adjudicate
enumerate every entry point, source and sink before touching one
turn a source-to-sink lead into a confirmed finding or a documented kill
TOCTOU, check-then-act, atomicity, lock misuse (credits, balances, webhooks)
step-skip, limit/price overflow, replay, paywall/entitlement bypass
UAF, double-free, OOB, uninitialized, NULL deref
find the unguarded peer of a guarded function
nonce reuse, key recovery, padding oracles, length extension
controls that allow on error, empty allowlist, missing input, caught denial
is a dependency CVE actually reachable from your code, or noise
dependency confusion, slopsquatting, poisoned CI, pipeline privilege
hallucinated imports, insecure defaults, claim-vs-behavior gaps
one confirmed bug → its siblings and the paths a fix missed
IDOR / BOLA — object ids parsed straight from requests
SQL/NoSQL injection through ORM/query-builder misuse
stored values that become queries later
Mongo/NoSQL operator and where-clause injection
shell/exec injection through args, filenames, redirects
../ and absolute-path escape to arbitrary file read/write
XSS in templates, sinks, and dangerous HTML APIs
SSTI → code execution through template engines
open redirect, target="_blank", forced navigation
CSRF and state-changing GET/unsafe methods
CORS misconfig, credentials + wildcard, origin reflection
session fixation, rotation on privilege change, expiry
JWT alg confusion, none alg, key trust, exp/aud validation
API key rotation, revocation, leak, scope
stack traces, verbose errors, source/secret leak in output
upload types, stored XSS, zip bombs, unvalidated MIME
framing, X-Frame-Options, CSP frame-ancestors
rate limits, abuse controls, enumeration vectors
what gets logged, integrity of the log, what's missing
Resend/Telnyx-style webhook signature verification + replay
payment state machine, idempotency, double-spend, refund abuse
secrets, storage, and debug interfaces in mobile clients
